summaryEn: One of Taiwan's largest brokers not owned by a financial holding company — and the most cyclical business in this collection. It earned NT$0.39 per share in the bear market of 2022 and NT$1.34 in the first quarter of 2026 alone. Its reported dividend yield does not reconcile, and has been removed.
model: editorial (truth-audited: FinMind + StatementDog + press; brokerage framing — the trading-volume leverage, 15.94% ROE and 2026Q1 surge credited, but extreme cyclicality documented from the company's own record (FY2022 EPS 0.39 versus 2026Q1 alone at 1.34; dividend NT$1.65 to NT$0.39) and the 86.6% debt ratio explained as a broker's normal structure rather than distress; a provably inconsistent dividendYield field was verified against two independent sources and STRIPPED, with the unexplained FY2025 payout anomaly disclosed rather than resolved; sector Financials → Securities Brokerage)

sections.bodyMarkdown:
Capital Securities (群益金鼎證券, TWSE: 6005) is a securities firm — it executes trades for clients, lends them money to buy shares on margin, underwrites offerings, and trades on its own account. Founded in **1988** and **listed in November 2005**, it is one of the larger Taiwanese brokers that is **not owned by a financial holding company**, which makes it an unusually direct way to observe what a brokerage business actually does through a market cycle.

What it does is amplify. **In the bear market of 2022 the company earned NT$0.39 per share for the entire year** — including a loss in the second quarter. **In the first quarter of 2026 alone it earned NT$1.34.** Annual EPS ran **NT$0.39 (FY2022) → 1.89 (FY2023) → 2.25 (FY2024) → NT$2.64 (FY2025)**, and recent monthly revenue has been running **53% to 302%** above the prior year. Net profit in 2026Q1 was **NT$3.10bn against NT$1.00bn** a year earlier. Trailing **return on equity is 15.94%**.

None of that reflects a changing business. It reflects **Taiwanese stock market turnover**. A broker's revenue is commission on trading volume, interest on margin lending, and gains on its own positions — all three rise together in a bull market and fall together in a bear one, against a cost base of branches, systems and staff that does not move nearly as much. That is the entire model, and it is why **this is the most cyclical company in this collection**.

At **NT$33.70 the shares trade at 9.41× earnings and 1.52× book**. The **86.6% debt ratio** is not distress — it is the normal structure of a securities firm, whose liabilities are largely client balances and financing for trading and margin positions. Similarly, **2026Q1 operating cash flow of −NT$5.37bn against +NT$3.10bn of net income** reflects capital deployed into trading and margin lending, not cash burn.

**One reported figure has been removed from this page.** The data feed showed a **dividend yield of 5.07%**, which at NT$33.70 implies a dividend near **NT$1.71**. But the **FY2025 cash dividend is NT$0.4** according to both the same feed's dividend series and an independent source, and NT$0.4 ÷ NT$33.70 is about **1.2%** — matching that source's stated 1.22%. The **yield field is therefore wrong and has been stripped**. Separately verified: **the FY2024 dividend of NT$1.5 went ex on 17 June 2025 and was paid on 14 July 2025**, and the company has paid dividends for **17 consecutive years totalling NT$13.48**, historically at a payout of **around 65–70%**. **The NT$0.4 FY2025 figure does not fit that pattern against EPS of NT$2.64, and this page does not attempt to explain it** — readers should confirm the FY2025 distribution from company filings.

The honest read: **a well-run, unaffiliated broker earning excellent returns in a strong market — where the single most important question is not how good the company is, but where the market cycle is.**

Capital Securities was founded in **1988**, at the height of Taiwan's first great stock market boom. The TAIEX rose more than tenfold in the late 1980s before collapsing by roughly 80% in 1990 — an episode that taught the industry, permanently, what its business actually is.

Brokerage is a simple model with violent operating leverage. A securities firm earns **commission on the value of shares it executes**, **interest on money it lends clients to buy shares on margin**, **fees from underwriting and corporate finance**, and **gains or losses on securities it holds itself**. Against that it carries **branches, trading systems, compliance and staff** — costs that are largely fixed. When trading volumes double, revenue roughly doubles and most of the increase falls to profit. When volumes halve, the same arithmetic runs backwards.

Taiwan's brokerage industry consolidated substantially over the following decades, with most large brokers absorbed into **financial holding companies** — Yuanta, Fubon, CTBC and others, several of which appear in this collection. Capital Securities remained **independent of a financial holding structure**, which is why its results show the brokerage cycle without the smoothing that banking or insurance earnings provide inside a holding group. It **listed in 2005**.

The record since is the cycle written plainly. **FY2022** — a bear market year — produced **NT$0.39 of EPS for the whole year**, including a **loss in the second quarter**, and the dividend fell to **NT$0.39** from NT$1.65. Then Taiwanese trading volumes recovered and rose sharply, and earnings followed: **NT$1.89, NT$2.25, NT$2.64**, and **NT$1.34 in the first quarter of 2026 alone** — more than three times the whole of 2022.

That is not a company transforming itself. It is a company doing the same thing while the market around it changes. Understanding Capital Securities means understanding that its earnings are, to a first approximation, **a leveraged bet on Taiwanese stock market activity**.

- **1988 (21 June)** — Capital Securities founded, during Taiwan's late-1980s stock market boom.
- **1990s–2000s** — Taiwan's brokerage industry consolidates, with most large brokers absorbed into **financial holding companies**; Capital Securities remains independent of one.
- **2005 (21 Nov)** — **Lists on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (6005)**.
- **2021** — A strong market year; dividend of **NT$1.65**.
- **2022** — **A bear market.** Full-year EPS of **NT$0.39**, including a **loss of NT$0.12 in Q2**; dividend cut to **NT$0.39**.
- **2023** — Recovery: **FY2023 EPS NT$1.89**; dividend **NT$1.33**.
- **2024** — **FY2024 EPS NT$2.25**; dividend **NT$1.5** (ex-dividend **17 June 2025**, paid **14 July 2025**).
- **2025** — **FY2025 EPS NT$2.64**, with the second half far stronger than the first (Q3 **NT$0.94**, Q4 **NT$0.77**). Recorded FY2025 dividend **NT$0.4** — a figure that does not fit the company's historical **65–70% payout** and is disclosed here without explanation.
- **2026Q1** — **EPS NT$1.34** — more than three times the whole of FY2022 — on net profit of **NT$3.10bn** against **NT$1.00bn** a year earlier. Monthly revenue runs **+53% to +302%** year-on-year. Trailing **ROE 15.94%**.
- **Cumulative record** — dividends paid for **17 consecutive years, totalling NT$13.48**.

Capital Securities' accounts are **the clearest demonstration of operating leverage in this collection** — and contain one figure that had to be removed.

- **Earnings that move with the market, violently.** Annual EPS: **NT$0.39 (FY2022) → 1.89 (FY2023) → 2.25 (FY2024) → NT$2.64 (FY2025)**, and **2026Q1 alone at NT$1.34**. The 2022 figure included a **quarterly loss of NT$0.12**. A single recent quarter earned more than three times an entire bear-market year — on the same branches, the same systems and broadly the same staff.
- **The current surge is exceptional.** **2026Q1 net profit of NT$3.10bn against NT$1.00bn** a year earlier, with monthly revenue running **+130%, +54%, +53%, +302%, +156%, +101%** across recent months. Trailing **return on equity is 15.94%**.
- **The balance sheet looks alarming and is not.** **NT$393.2bn of assets** against **NT$52.9bn of equity** — an **86.6% debt ratio**. For a securities firm this is normal structure: liabilities are largely **client balances, repurchase agreements and financing for trading and margin-lending positions**, not corporate borrowing to fund operations. The same is true of **2026Q1 operating cash flow of −NT$5.37bn against +NT$3.10bn of net income** — capital was deployed into positions, which is what a broker does in a rising market.
- **No margin data is reported, correctly.** Gross, operating and net margins are manufacturing concepts and the feed supplies none for this company. None have been invented here.
- **A dividend field that does not reconcile, and what was done about it.** The data feed reported a **5.07% dividend yield**, implying a dividend near **NT$1.71** at NT$33.70. But the **FY2025 cash dividend is NT$0.4** — per the same feed's dividend series and per an independent source — and **NT$0.4 ÷ NT$33.70 ≈ 1.2%**, matching that source's stated **1.22%**. **The yield field is inconsistent with the dividend data and has been removed from this page.**
- **The dividend record, verified separately.** **NT$1.65 (2021) → NT$0.39 (2022) → 1.33 (2023) → NT$1.5 (2024)**, with the FY2024 payment going **ex on 17 June 2025 and paid 14 July 2025**. **17 consecutive years of dividends totalling NT$13.48**, at a payout historically **around 65–70%**. **The recorded FY2025 figure of NT$0.4 against EPS of NT$2.64 is a roughly 15% payout, which does not fit** — and this page discloses that anomaly rather than resolving it.
- **Valuation.** **9.41× earnings and 1.52× book** — a low multiple, which is the market's standard treatment of peak-cycle brokerage earnings.

The financing reality: **a broker earning strongly in a strong market, structurally sound despite an alarming-looking debt ratio, with one reported figure removed for being demonstrably wrong and one payout anomaly left openly unexplained.**

**Stance: an independent, well-run broker earning 15.94% on equity in a strong Taiwanese market at 9.41x earnings — and the single most cycle-dependent business in this collection.**

The bull case:

1. **Powerful operating leverage in a rising market.** Commission, margin-lending interest and proprietary trading gains all rise together while branch, systems and staff costs do not. **2026Q1 EPS of NT$1.34** against **NT$0.39 for the whole of FY2022** shows the amplitude.
2. **Independence gives a clean exposure.** Most large Taiwanese brokers sit inside financial holding companies where banking and insurance earnings dilute the effect. Capital Securities offers the brokerage cycle directly — which is a feature for anyone who wants that exposure.
3. **A low multiple and a long dividend record.** **9.41× earnings, 1.52× book**, and **17 consecutive years of dividends totalling NT$13.48**, at a payout historically around **65–70%**.
4. **Sound structure.** The **86.6% debt ratio** is client balances and trading finance, not corporate leverage; **NT$52.9bn of equity** backs **NT$393.2bn of assets**.

The counter-arguments:

- **The earnings are the cycle.** **FY2022 EPS was NT$0.39.** A single bear-market year can remove roughly 85% of the earnings — and the low P/E exists precisely because the market knows this. **Buying a broker at a low multiple on peak earnings is the classic error in this industry.**
- **Everything depends on trading volume**, which depends on market direction and sentiment — not on management.
- **The dividend follows immediately.** **NT$1.65 (2021) → NT$0.39 (2022).** There is no smoothing.
- **A reported dividend anomaly is unresolved.** The FY2025 payout of **NT$0.4 against NT$2.64 of EPS** does not match the historical 65–70%, and the reported yield field was wrong enough to remove.
- **No diversification.** Unlike a financial holding company, there is no banking or insurance earnings stream to offset a weak market.

A **cycle-timing** thesis: an honest, well-capitalised broker offering exactly what it says — the question is entirely about where Taiwanese trading volumes go next.

Capital Securities earns money from **stock market activity**, in four related ways:

- **Brokerage commission.** A percentage of the value of every trade executed for clients. This scales **directly with market turnover** — if daily trading value doubles, commission roughly doubles, with almost no additional cost.
- **Margin lending.** Lending clients money to buy shares, secured against those shares, and earning interest. Margin balances **expand in rising markets and contract in falling ones**, so this income is doubly cyclical — and it carries credit risk if a sharp fall leaves collateral insufficient.
- **Proprietary trading and investment.** Positions taken with the firm's own capital. This produces gains in good markets and losses in bad ones, and is the reason a broker can post an outright quarterly loss, as happened in **2022Q2**.
- **Underwriting and corporate finance.** Fees from bringing companies to market and arranging capital raising. **Issuance activity itself is cyclical** — companies list when markets are strong.
- **Why the leverage is so extreme.** The cost base is **branches, trading platforms, compliance and staff** — largely fixed. Revenue moves with market turnover. So a doubling of activity produces far more than a doubling of profit, and a halving produces far more than a halving. **NT$0.39 for all of FY2022 against NT$1.34 in 2026Q1 alone** is that arithmetic in practice.
- **What the balance sheet actually contains.** **NT$393.2bn of assets** against **NT$52.9bn of equity**. The liabilities are predominantly **client cash balances, repurchase financing and funding for margin loans and trading positions** — the working inventory of a securities business, not debt raised to run the company.

The levers are **Taiwanese market turnover, margin loan balances, proprietary trading results and underwriting activity** — and all four move together. The strength is genuine operating leverage and a long dividend record. The vulnerability is that **there is no counter-cyclical earnings stream anywhere in the business**: when the market falls, every revenue line falls at once.

Taiwanese securities broking is a consolidated, intensely cyclical industry attached to one of the world's most actively traded retail markets.

- **The structure.** Most large Taiwanese brokers were absorbed into **financial holding companies** — **Yuanta, Fubon, CTBC, KGI** and others, several of which appear in this collection. Inside a holding group, brokerage earnings are blended with banking and insurance, smoothing the cycle. **Capital Securities is one of the larger firms that remained independent**, which is why its results display the cycle in isolation.
- **Why Taiwan's market amplifies it.** Taiwan has an unusually **high level of retail participation** and turnover relative to market capitalisation, and a well-developed **margin lending** market. Both make brokerage revenue more volatile than in markets dominated by institutional, low-turnover investors.
- **What competition looks like.** Commission rates in Taiwan have been competed down over years, and discount brokerage and online platforms continue to pressure them. Brokers respond by growing **wealth management, margin lending, derivatives and proprietary trading** — moving from pure execution toward balance-sheet and advisory income.
- **The cycle's amplitude.** The industry's earnings swing enormously with market conditions: **Capital Securities earned NT$0.39 in FY2022 and NT$1.34 in 2026Q1 alone**. Nothing about the industry's structure dampens this — it is the defining characteristic.
- **How the market prices it.** Brokers trade on **low multiples at cycle peaks and high multiples at troughs**, because investors know current earnings are unrepresentative. **9.41× earnings** for a company earning **15.94% on equity** is not a bargain overlooked; it is the market applying a cyclical discount.

Capital Securities' position is **solid within an industry whose fortunes it does not control**. The industry truth is that **a broker's competitive quality determines its share of trading, and the market determines how much trading there is** — and the second variable dominates the first by a wide margin.

**Strengths**
- **Strong operating leverage**: **2026Q1 EPS NT$1.34** against **NT$0.39 for all of FY2022**; **ROE 15.94%**.
- **Independent of a financial holding company** — a direct, unblended brokerage exposure.
- **17 consecutive years of dividends totalling NT$13.48**, historically at a **65–70% payout**.
- **Sound structure**: **NT$52.9bn of equity**; the 86.6% debt ratio is client balances and trading finance, not corporate borrowing.

**Weaknesses**
- **Extreme cyclicality** — every revenue line moves together with market turnover.
- **FY2022 EPS of NT$0.39** including a quarterly loss; dividend fell to **NT$0.39** the same year.
- **No counter-cyclical earnings** — no banking or insurance to offset a weak market.
- **A reported dividend yield was demonstrably wrong and removed**; the FY2025 payout anomaly is unresolved.

**Opportunities**
- Continued strength in Taiwanese trading volumes and margin balances.
- Growth in **wealth management, derivatives and advisory** income, which is less turnover-dependent.
- Potential consolidation value as an independent broker in a consolidated industry.

**Threats**
- **A market downturn** collapsing commission, margin interest and trading gains simultaneously.
- **Commission rate competition** from discount and online platforms.
- **Margin lending credit losses** in a sharp market fall.

- **A bear market removes most of the earnings (the defining risk).** **FY2022 produced NT$0.39 of EPS for the entire year, including a quarterly loss**, against **NT$1.34 in 2026Q1 alone**. Commission, margin interest, trading gains and underwriting fees all fall together, against a largely fixed cost base. The **9.41× multiple** is low precisely because current earnings are unlikely to be representative.
- **The dividend collapses with earnings.** **NT$1.65 (2021) → NT$0.39 (2022).** There is no reserve mechanism smoothing distributions through the cycle.
- **A reported figure was wrong, and another is unexplained.** The feed's **5.07% dividend yield** could not be reconciled with a **NT$0.4** FY2025 dividend at **NT$33.70** (about 1.2%), and **has been removed**. Separately, that **NT$0.4 against EPS of NT$2.64** is roughly a **15% payout**, well outside the company's historical **65–70%** range — an anomaly disclosed here without explanation. **Verify the FY2025 distribution from company filings.**
- **Margin lending is credit risk in disguise.** Loans secured by shares are safe until the shares fall sharply and quickly. Margin balances are largest exactly when the market is most extended.
- **Proprietary trading can produce outright losses**, as 2022Q2 showed — this is not a fee-only business.
- **Structural commission pressure.** Rate competition from discount and online brokers erodes the core execution margin over time, independent of the cycle.

Capital Securities' outlook is, unusually candidly, **a question about the Taiwanese stock market rather than about the company.** The axes to watch:

- **Market turnover.** The dominant variable. Monthly revenue running **+53% to +302%** reflects exceptional trading activity. Whether that persists determines earnings more than any management decision.
- **Full-year EPS against the cycle's range.** The record runs from **NT$0.39 (FY2022)** to **NT$2.64 (FY2025)**, with **2026Q1 at NT$1.34**. Judging this company means placing the current year within that range, not extrapolating from it.
- **Margin lending balances.** Both a revenue driver and a risk indicator. Rising balances signal strong activity; they also signal rising credit exposure if the market turns.
- **The FY2025 dividend.** The recorded **NT$0.4** against **NT$2.64 of EPS** is inconsistent with a **65–70% historical payout**, and the reported yield field was wrong enough to remove. The declared FY2025 distribution — confirmed from company filings — is the figure to rely on.
- **Fee income that is less turnover-dependent.** Growth in **wealth management and advisory** would structurally reduce the amplitude, which is the only strategic lever available.

Bottom line: Capital Securities is a well-capitalised, independent broker earning **15.94% on equity** at **9.41× earnings and 1.52× book**, with **17 consecutive years of dividends**. It is also the **most cycle-dependent business in this collection**: it earned **NT$0.39 in the whole of 2022** and **NT$1.34 in a single quarter of 2026**, with **no counter-cyclical earnings anywhere in the business**. One reported figure — the dividend yield — was **demonstrably inconsistent and has been removed**, and the FY2025 payout anomaly is **disclosed rather than explained**. Judge it on **where Taiwanese trading volumes are in their cycle** — the company is sound; the earnings are borrowed from the market.
